requirements.clause:
1. **Package and import isolation:** build and pack real artifacts; install outside workspace linking in vanilla and React/Next consumers. Check emitted imports, declared exports/types, external React peers, zero core runtime dependencies, selective entry size and truthful registration side effects. Import server/helper entries with browser globals absent and verify no registration/observer/frame work starts.
2. **Renderer experiment before commitment:** compare equivalent distinctive visuals using DOM/CSS, SVG where appropriate, and inherited canvas candidates. Record compressed import sizes, mount/update work, frame traces, node counts, buffer/backing-store memory and many-instance behavior on declared hardware/browser versions. Include visible, offscreen, zero-size, paused/reduced-motion and static scenarios. Preserve intended visual quality and choose the simplest sufficient implementation; do not infer a win from one RAF loop. Numerical budgets and representative fixture counts are owned by the performance ticket.
3. **SSR/DSD/React integration before claiming support:** exercise server-ready and pending markup, delayed/disabled JavaScript, DSD present/absent, Next initial HTML and streamed/client navigation paths. Verify useful first paint, reserved geometry, preserved light-DOM nodes, repeatable registration/property delivery, Strict Mode lifecycle, deterministic initial presentation and no unexplained hydration warnings. Do not hide unproven hydration behavior behind blanket warning suppression or disable SSR as a workaround for the public contract.
4. **Lifecycle, race and resource evidence:** repeat mount/remove/reconnect and same-origin adoption; test multiple independent regions, nested scrolling and multiple compatible runtime users. Verify latest-intent handling, no late obsolete presentation, suspended decorative work when hidden/offscreen/still, service teardown at last consumer, bounded retained memory and no interference between documents or server requests. Numeric memory thresholds are for the performance ticket.
5. **Styling, fallback and content-access integration:** exercise scoped theme tokens, selected public parts, application/Tailwind styling on host/content, static fallback and the chosen stylesheet strategy under the documented CSP policy. Validate missing optional rendering capabilities and decorative failures against current application intent: ready content stays usable, pending content has a useful static presentation, and obsolete/unready content is not exposed. Detailed CSP/customization guarantees belong to the API ticket; focus/live-region/manual assistive-technology requirements belong to the accessibility ticket. These decisions must be settled before implementation relies on style/HTML sinks.
6. **Support-floor and full readiness-contract verification:** run distributable consumers on declared browser floors/current stable, React minimum/current supported lines and Next 16 App Router; supplement automated engines with real Safari/iOS. Run the full approved [v1 readiness acceptance scenarios](https://github.com/b4rb13/dot-loaders/issues/5#issuecomment-6204621037), not just static component screenshots. Publish only the matrix actually verified.

requirements.clause: Target WCAG 2.2 AA for the website and accessible integrations. Core/React release checks cover accessible presentation-state handling, decorative rendering, hidden-content behavior, motion support and documented integration patterns. The website owns complete navigation, examples, playground controls and loading flows. Consumers own meaningful content, labels, localized status messages, error recovery and application-specific focus destinations. Document tested combinations and consumer responsibilities; package checks are not a claim that every consuming page/process conforms.

requirements.clause: Skeletons, animated dots, chart silhouettes and table silhouettes are decorative. Expose no fake headings/cells/chart data or fabricated progress percentages. Hide the decorative surface from assistive technology while preserving the meaningful content semantics of LoadingRegion/TextLoader.

requirements.clause: The library-controlled content boundary is busy in pending and refreshing, and no longer busy when ready without waiting for decorative completion. Pending content remains mounted when supplied but is hidden/unavailable for interaction; refresh keeps useful content visible/interactable; ready makes the current outcome available. Preserve authored host attributes and avoid automatically making every region a landmark. Exact focus/hidden mechanics follow in the focus round.

requirements.clause: Application composition supplies one meaningful, localized status message for the relevant operation, using a stable role=status element outside the busy/hidden subtree when appropriate. It is polite/atomic and does not take focus. No automatic per-skeleton, per-frame, cycle-ID or generic Loaded narration. Applications choose useful result, empty/error and recovery messages.

requirements.clause: Preserve focus unless its owner is about to become unavailable. Applications may move focus to a meaningful destination before declaring pending, such as the filter that triggered replacement. If focus remains inside content the library is about to hide, move focus to the stable LoadingRegion host before hiding/inerting that subtree. Preserve supplied content instances. If focus is already outside the disappearing content, leave it alone; skeleton shapes are never focus destinations.

requirements.clause: Document LoadingRegion host defaults for this fallback: programmatic focus through tabindex=-1 and a non-landmark group role, preserving explicit author values. Applications should supply a meaningful accessible name, such as Account activity. The fallback needs visible focus. These are deliberate accessibility host defaults supplementing the accepted API; no new focus-callback prop or application-wide focus manager is introduced.

requirements.section: Readiness does not restore or steal focus
requirements.clause: When content becomes ready, keep focus at its current location. Do not automatically restore an old control or focus the first result. A user who has moved elsewhere is not pulled back by completion. Refresh preserves focus in content that remains interactive. Initial loading, success, empty/error/cancellation outcomes do not independently trigger focus movement; applications may deliberately focus headings/retry buttons/validation messages for their workflows. Ready content becomes keyboard-accessible without waiting for decorative completion. Announcements remain separate from focus.
requirements.responsibleRole: implementing maintainer; owner for product/access/release decisions

requirements.clause: Applications coordinate open modal dialogs before replacing their containing content: a modal can escape ancestor inertness and an outside region anchor cannot receive focus while that modal is active. The library does not independently dismiss dialogs or override their focus manager. Applications also choose a meaningful destination when they intentionally remove a focused component.
requirements.responsibleRole: implementing maintainer; owner for product/access/release decisions

requirements.clause: Library fallback handling must account for slotted/nested Web Component focus, recheck current intent after focus handlers, avoid traps/repeated focus attempts/delayed restoration callbacks, and diagnose unavailable fallback destinations with documented integration requirements. Do not claim DOM focus management controls every assistive-technology virtual cursor.

requirements.section: Reduced motion is live and authoritative
requirements.clause: Reduced motion makes all library-owned loading effects static and settles handoffs immediately to the latest valid presentation. Apply it from first presentation, including server-rendered examples, and respond to changes while the page is open. motion=paused has the same static presentation behavior. A child or preset cannot override an ancestor pause or OS reduced motion.
requirements.responsibleRole: implementing maintainer; owner for product/access/release decisions

requirements.section: Reduced motion is live and authoritative
requirements.clause: Loading state, available content, focus, busy metadata and application status messages continue normally. Returning to normal motion can resume an eligible pending effect within its remaining activity window; it never replays ready content. Preserve the already-approved presentation event/intent rules when settling handoffs.

requirements.section: Persistent user preference belongs to the application
requirements.clause: The website provides a clearly labeled, keyboard-operable Pause animations control outside loading content, persisted across navigation/reloads. Documentation supplies a reusable consumer recipe using the existing motion API. Applications own persistence and pass paused to their regions/loaders, applying a saved pause before animation begins. Core performs no automatic storage access and requires no global provider.

requirements.section: Persistent user preference belongs to the application
requirements.clause: Pausing stops decoration, not requests/content updates/status messages. Re-enabling still honors OS reduced motion. A programmatic prop alone is not a user-operable control; hover-only/focus-only pauses are insufficient.

requirements.clause: All v1 families share the product rule: a continuous automatic loading presentation has a maximum four-second motion window, covering loading activity and its handoff, then becomes static while loading remains pending. The deadline overrides longer timing.duration requests and cannot be extended by speed. Changing cycle during continuous loading, changing styles, pausing or toggling visibility does not grant a new four-second window. An exhausted window stays static; readiness later presents the outcome immediately. There is no artificial timeout, cancellation, success or error outcome at the motion deadline.
requirements.responsibleRole: implementing maintainer; owner for product/access/release decisions

requirements.clause: Applications own genuine long-wait messages, timeouts, retries and cancellation. Examples must not repeatedly remount loaders to create automatic replay. A playground may offer an explicit Replay demo action that still respects pause/OS preferences. Do not infer whole-application compliance for repeated automatic information updates from this bounded decorative effect rule.
requirements.responsibleRole: implementing maintainer; owner for product/access/release decisions

requirements.clause: Validate actual displayed stopping, including compositor motion during main-thread stalls; a JavaScript timer intention alone is insufficient evidence. The four-second value is an approved accessibility/product bound, not a performance measurement or a mandatory loading duration.
requirements.responsibleRole: implementing maintainer; owner for product/access/release decisions

requirements.clause: Built-in treatments adapt to user color settings and remain safe within the supported customization range. Respect system colors and keep loading shapes/focus distinguishable. Canvas explicitly adapts or uses a static DOM fallback rather than assuming CSS recolors existing pixels. Avoid broad forced-color-adjust:none opt-outs.

requirements.clause: Website text/status messages meet 4.5:1 contrast, or 3:1 for large text; necessary graphical indicators/custom control boundaries meet applicable 3:1 requirements. Pure decoration is not assigned a blanket per-dot contrast ratio, but meaningful loading information stays perceivable. Consumers own selected palettes. Loading/error/focus information must remain understandable without color alone.

requirements.clause: Built-ins avoid strobing. All allowed speeds/presets and simultaneous surfaces must satisfy flashing requirements independently of the four-second motion deadline. Unsafe configurations are constrained or fall back to static presentation.

requirements.clause: Defaults, docs and playground support 200% text resizing, ordinary-layout reflow at 400% zoom/320 CSS pixels, user text-spacing overrides, long translations, RTL/mixed-direction text, emoji and combining characters without losing content/function. Meaningfully two-dimensional tables/charts may use appropriate local scrolling; surrounding messages/controls/page are not blanket exceptions.

requirements.clause: Preserve supplied text, lang and dir. Unsupported glyph effects use the approved generic/simple reveal; never manually reverse RTL text or substitute characters to fit decoration. Resize/font changes update measurements without new loading or indefinite waiting. Direction changes preserve the documented geometry-coordinate contract. Consumer-imposed dimensions/colors remain documented integration responsibilities.

requirements.clause: Ready server content remains readable with normal semantics. Pending server markup includes static loading presentation/accessible explanation while unready content stays unavailable. Client-only data has an application-owned persistent explanation and appropriate recovery/navigation route that works without hydration. Delayed/failed enhancement preserves the valid static presentation and existing supplied content. Enhancement preserves identity and does not replay already-ready content.

requirements.clause: Test disabled scripts, failed modules, delayed hydration and failed upgrades separately: noscript alone misses enabled-but-failed scripts. Missing JavaScript never fabricates readiness/success/error. Applications own fallback wording/recovery; recipes show this concretely.

requirements.section: Supporting details for the approved visual requirements
requirements.clause: For ordinary layouts, verify 200% text resize and reflow at a 320 CSS-pixel viewport, including an actual desktop 400% zoom check. Text-spacing override checks use 1.5 line height, 2 times paragraph spacing, 0.12em letter spacing and 0.16em word spacing where applicable; these are user-override tests, not required design defaults. Long translations and actual mixed-script/RTL/emoji/combining fixtures must preserve logical content, reading order and author lang/dir. Do not change the geometry bridge's content-box pixel origin or infer business-data ordering from direction.
requirements.responsibleRole: implementing maintainer; owner for product/access/release decisions

requirements.section: Supporting details for the approved visual requirements
requirements.clause: Use system foreground/background pairs in forced colors. Preserve user-selected colors even if they differ from the design palette; the default-theme contrast targets are not permission to defeat user color settings. Test genuine Windows forced colors, not only emulated media. Verify necessary outlines/borders and current focus remain distinguishable when shadows/background effects are removed. Public styles/presets may not bypass the library's motion/flashing safeguards. Arbitrary consumer CSS/custom components and palettes remain consumer-owned, with documented limits rather than an unconditional safety claim.
requirements.responsibleRole: implementing maintainer; owner for product/access/release decisions

requirements.section: Supporting details for the approved visual requirements
requirements.clause: The flash gate covers supported speed boundaries, all built-in effects and simultaneous surfaces against SC 2.3.1 (no more than three flashes in any one-second interval unless below the applicable general/red-flash thresholds). The product preference is no strobing. Brief animation is not an exemption. If necessary, constrain a customization or use static presentation; never expose an unsafe allowed configuration merely because it is fast or short.
requirements.responsibleRole: implementing maintainer; owner for product/access/release decisions

requirements.clause: The four-second maximum is elapsed time from the first automatic motion in one continuously active loading presentation, including any handoff. It is not scaled by speed and does not count from the start of a network request. Child decorative participants in the same owning region use that region's remaining window; mounting another placeholder inside an exhausted owner cannot grant more motion. Independently controlled regions retain independent readiness/presentation ownership, with ancestor pause restrictions as already approved.
requirements.responsibleRole: implementing maintainer; owner for product/access/release decisions

requirements.clause: Pause, offscreen/tab hiding, cycle changes during continuous loading, and disconnect/reconnect of the same instance do not renew the window. No decorative frames are required while suspended; elapsed time can still exhaust the window. If no motion has yet started, a static server render does not itself consume four seconds of animation. On expiry, loading stays pending/busy and useful static presentation remains; a later ready outcome is available immediately without another automatic reveal animation. A handoff interrupted by the deadline settles the latest valid presentation with the approved terminal event semantics.
requirements.responsibleRole: implementing maintainer; owner for product/access/release decisions

requirements.clause: A genuinely settled ready presentation followed by a distinct application loading presentation may start a new window. A skipped/coalesced ready value or supersession during a handoff does not. This does not define a universal WCAG-safe gap for repeated effects. New instances do not gain global cross-mount history; consumers own repeated automatic remounts, polling and auto-updating information, and provide usable controls for the overall composed behavior where required. Our recipes never use remount churn to evade the limit. An explicit Replay demo action may create a fresh demonstration without defeating persisted pause or OS preferences. No new infinite-loop, motion-budget override or force-animation API is introduced in v1.

requirements.clause:
1. **Distributable fixtures and state coverage.** Test actual packed native, React and Next consumers with the same public configuration used in docs. Cover every family and loading state, instant handoff, zero/empty/error/cancel outcomes, interruption, reconnect and nested/independent ownership. Include declared supported CSS/CSP delivery modes and static server output. No test-only application wrapper may hide a production integration problem.
2. **Automated checks plus human assessment.** Run appropriate automated accessibility scans and DOM/keyboard/focus/hidden-state assertions in meaningful pending, refreshing, handoff and settled/error states. Use axe-core or equivalent as development-only tooling. Zero detected scan violations is not AA certification. Human keyboard, visual and AT assessment remains mandatory. The website also receives a complete applicable WCAG 2.2 A/AA review of navigation, headings, labels, names/roles/values, controls and end-to-end flows; loader fixtures alone cannot establish full-site conformance.
3. **Keyboard/focus safety.** Verify ordinary Tab/Shift+Tab, visible/unobscured focus, host fallback defaults and preserved authored role/tabindex, slotted/open-shadow content and closed hosts treated as opaque focus owners. Move before hiding; aria-hidden or opacity alone is not keyboard protection. Never expose hidden controls, focus a skeleton, trap navigation or restore stale focus. Exercise reentrant focus handlers and intent changes. Modal/intentional-removal recipes must demonstrate application coordination.
4. **Meaningful feedback and exposure.** Inspect actual accessibility exposure and listen with each required AT combination. Check accurate busy state, application-supplied localized status outside busy/hidden subtrees, real text once, no fake table/chart semantics, no repeated decorative announcements or stale outcomes. Assert meaningful information and usable interaction, not identical spoken strings or arbitrary speech timing across readers. No promise to programmatically control every virtual cursor.
5. **Motion and pause evidence.** Verify OS preference at first paint and runtime changes, saved pause before enhancement, keyboard-operable persistent website control, nested restrictions, remaining-window resume, and readiness/events during pause. Measure actual four-second displayed stop and large-duration/speed boundary cases, including compositor motion during main-thread stalls. Static/no-frame states still process readiness and necessary events. Screenshots/timeout callbacks alone are insufficient proof.
6. **Colors, flash and layout evidence.** Test light/dark/nested themes, genuine forced colors, necessary contrast and focus, no color-only status, maximum supported effect speeds/multiple surfaces, actual text resize/zoom, narrow reflow, spacing overrides and international fixtures. Use appropriate frame/flash analysis for effects; a scan or four-second cap does not establish flash safety. No lost text, controls or recovery actions under the supported presentation contract.
7. **Static, failed enhancement and CSP.** Test server-ready/pending HTML, disabled JS, failed modules, delayed hydration, failed registration/renderer enhancement and chosen DSD fallback. Useful content/status and required hiding/inert behavior must hold before upgrade, not be repaired only after hydration. Test real approved CSP headers. Application fallback explanation/navigation remains operable without script, never relies solely on noscript and never reveals obsolete/unready content or fabricates an outcome.
8. **Evidence and release blocking.** Record package/build and fixture, date, OS/browser/AT versions/settings, real device where applicable, steps, expected/observed behavior, results and limitations. Required cells are pass/fail/unverified. A failure or missing evidence blocks the affected release/support claim; fix with evidence, or return a guarantee/support change for explicit approval. Do not waive an observed accessibility failure with documentation alone. Browser quirks can use a verified fallback that satisfies the contract. Publish only actually verified combinations, with wording consistent with the declared support contract.

requirements.section: Approved clarification 1 — reproducible measurement and comparison

requirements.section: Approved clarification 1 — reproducible measurement and comparison
requirements.clause: Use three warmups separate from twenty valid measured runs. Initialization/handoff have their own phases. Benchmark replay is an isolated measurement operation, not an application recipe for bypassing the motion limit. Alternate or balance static/animated runs under the fixed protocol. Keep ordinary GC, workload-induced throttling, valid slow runs and maxima; only predefined external protocol failures invalidate a run, and invalid attempts/reasons remain recorded.

Use max(0, A[i] - S[i]) as the conservative additional-work estimate. Preserve both raw traces, signed differences, whole-page frame health and event attribution. Browser trace methods and phase/bin boundaries are part of the manifest. If an environment cannot provide comparable evidence, mark the affected metric unverified rather than substituting scheduler callback duration.

requirements.section: Approved clarification 1 — reproducible measurement and comparison
requirements.clause: Use nearest-rank percentiles. For initialization/registration/server render, p95 across twenty run totals is the nineteenth sorted value. Rendering computes p95/p99 from frame estimates within each run; at least eighteen of twenty runs must satisfy BOTH limits, and pooled p95/p99 must also satisfy them. Report all per-run tails and pooled results; correlated frames do not become twenty independent statistical proofs. Any introduced task of 50ms or more independently fails regardless of percentile results. Confirm attribution against traces/static baseline; absent LoAF entries or smooth compositor-only movement is not sufficient proof. The 30-updates/second floor applies only to intended continuously animated dense presentation under normal motion conditions, measured by meaningful rendered cadence; it never requires JS loops for CSS-driven or inherently static primitives. Declared stress/static/reduced/paused modes are exempt but disclosed. Time-based motion remains correct at changed cadence.
requirements.responsibleRole: implementing maintainer; owner for product/access/release decisions

requirements.section: Approved clarification 1 — reproducible measurement and comparison
requirements.clause: The Pixel reference owns the hard timing ceilings. M1/iPhone runs retain compatibility and regression evidence without claiming the Pixel result proves every device. All architecture browser floors/current versions and accessibility matrix remain binding for their approved functional gates. Missing reference hardware/required tooling leaves a gate unverified. A 120Hz claim requires observed 120Hz behavior on a recorded separate profile; hardware advertising alone is insufficient. Its published 2/4ms and 4/6ms figures remain optimization goals until that profile is verified. Never silently substitute a faster device or relabel a 60Hz result.
requirements.responsibleRole: implementing maintainer; owner for product/access/release decisions

requirements.section: Approved clarification 2 — capacity, fallback and cleanup enforcement
requirements.clause: Resource ceilings are inclusive maxima, tested at and just beyond the boundary. The 50ms-task gate explicitly fails at equality. Apply effective DPR, per-axis and aggregate backing-pixel limits simultaneously, preserving CSS geometry/aspect ratio. A surface's backing budget includes all its library-owned canvases/snapshots/scratch backing; document totals include every compatible instance/copy in that document. Separate documents have separate ledgers. Pools, capacity slack, temporary resize/replacement storage and retained offscreen resources are charged before allocation; shared storage is counted once. Failed reservation/context creation releases its ledger reservation and uses a safe fallback without retry/allocation loops. A browser can still reject a below-cap allocation; caps do not guarantee GPU availability or bound all browser/process memory.
requirements.responsibleRole: implementing maintainer; owner for product/access/release decisions

requirements.section: Approved clarification 2 — capacity, fallback and cleanup enforcement
requirements.clause: Resolve table columns first (maximum twenty), then rows to min(requestedRows, 100, floor(1000 / resolvedColumnCount)); preserve positive defaults and diagnostics. All three caps therefore hold at once. Width fractions/column weights still follow the approved normalization. Lines/typing/geometry/dot limits bound decoration only. Fast source-length admission precedes expensive text processing; more than 256 specialized supported characters or unsupported Unicode uses generic treatment without truncating real text. Excess supplied arrays must not cause unbounded validation/copying; consume only bounded supported data and diagnose according to the API. Arbitrary application callback construction/execution is not preemptible; fixture providers are fixed, their calls/time/output included in the trace, and real application callback cost is disclosed separately from intrinsic guarantees.
requirements.responsibleRole: implementing maintainer; owner for product/access/release decisions

requirements.section: Approved clarification 2 — capacity, fallback and cleanup enforcement
requirements.clause: A provider is called at most twice during one active handoff; its opportunity is a bounded current-intent measurement attempt, not an indefinite promise of another paint. Two RAF callbacks alone are not proof of valid post-layout targets. Null/invalid/throwing/zero-size/hidden/unavailable geometry uses the approved simple fallback, never gates ready content, and cannot create a page barrier. Inactive/standalone surfaces do not poll unused providers. CPU/frame/resource constraints also apply to quality-control heuristics; no per-frame theme polling or catch-up backlog. Capacity returning may permit a later valid presentation to choose quality, but cannot replay ready content, renew the four-second window or oscillate the current presentation's quality.
requirements.responsibleRole: implementing maintainer; owner for product/access/release decisions

requirements.section: Approved clarification 2 — capacity, fallback and cleanup enforcement
requirements.clause: Heap gates use a fixed post-import/post-registration/post-warmup/teardown empty-fixture baseline on the pinned Chromium reference; measure live fixture increments in comparable lab conditions. Track explicit typed-array/backing capacities separately because heap does not establish GPU/total process memory. Nominal four-channel 8-bit pixel arithmetic is labeled an estimate. A clearRect call is not backing release; release unnecessary logical backing/storage with the appropriate renderer mechanism, without promising immediate GPU/RSS return.

requirements.section: Approved clarification 2 — capacity, fallback and cleanup enforcement
requirements.clause: For each of the three independent cleanup experiments, test the 24-surface cohort through 100 mount/update/handoff/removal cycles and check post-cleanup at 10, 50 and 100 against its fixed warm baseline. Every checkpoint in every repetition must stay within 512 KiB residual growth; do not average or choose the best repetition. Drop harness/application references before controlled lab GC and distinguish unavoidable registered code from discarded instances. Retained discarded instances/subtrees/callbacks/operational subscriptions fail regardless of byte count. No rising retained-instance/resource trend is accepted merely because heap remains below a numerical limit. Check disposal of every other fixture as well.
requirements.responsibleRole: implementing maintainer; owner for product/access/release decisions

requirements.section: Approved clarification 2 — capacity, fallback and cleanup enforcement
requirements.clause: After disconnection has been processed, cancel obsolete work and detach per-instance subscriptions; after the last service consumer leaves, operational listeners/observers/scheduled frames and unnecessary mutable buffers have no remaining library owner. Any already-delivered obsolete callback is inert and cannot reschedule or mutate presentation. Inactive mounted surfaces have no recurring decorative RAF/timer/polling loop, while required preference/resize/style/state events remain functional. Observe at least ten seconds of steady inactive state after pending one-shot events settle, alongside direct instrumentation of scheduled work; one event-driven coalesced redraw is distinct from a recurring animation loop. Reconnect, Strict Mode and same-origin adoption do not duplicate resources or apply old work; resource counts are checked directly, not inferred solely from GC.
requirements.responsibleRole: implementing maintainer; owner for product/access/release decisions

requirements.section: Approved clarification 3 — SSR, geometry and exception accounting
requirements.clause: The 1/2/16 KiB UTF-8 gates count each component's own non-style markup, excluding app content and separately counted nested library components. The 16 KiB limit is per maximum-supported component configuration, not the whole fixture. Default and maximum-input fixtures are both required. Whole-document accounting counts every actual nested contribution once; no per-dot serialization is needed merely to represent a useful static loading surface.
requirements.responsibleRole: implementing maintainer; owner for product/access/release decisions

requirements.section: Approved clarification 3 — SSR, geometry and exception accounting
requirements.clause: For the 24-surfaces/six-regions SSR case, use max(0, gzip(decoratedHTML) - gzip(matchedPlainHTML)) plus gzip bytes of unique additional required loader stylesheet responses on a cold style cache. Default embedded mode includes every repeated inline style/template/nonce/wrapper in the actual HTML. External mode counts every emitted link and required response; parsed CSS backing reuse or logical unique-CSS reports never deduct transmitted markup. Report actual raw and compressed documents/assets, markup breakdown and framework transport separately, without hand-picked omission of repeated output. The 8 KiB output, 12 KiB server code, 1/2/16 KiB raw markup and 20ms warm helper-time gates are independent. Real CSP modes and server-ready/pending/streamed paths remain covered by prior contracts.

requirements.section: Approved clarification 3 — SSR, geometry and exception accounting
requirements.clause: Geometry invariants concern host/content/neighbor layout in controlled fixed-size fixtures, not the expected movement of decorative particles. Record rectangles at static first paint, upgrade/hydration, readiness and handoff completion and inspect the raw shift entries including recent-input exclusions. The no-unintended-movement invariant and complete-scenario CLS <=0.01 are independent checks; neither excuses a failure of the other. Unknown final content/font/layout may resize naturally under the accepted caller-sizing policy, with the cause and observed result reported rather than claiming universal zero CLS.

requirements.section: Approved clarification 3 — SSR, geometry and exception accounting
requirements.clause: All ordinary cap/invariant failures block release. A numerical artifact/timing/live-heap target can receive ONLY the already-approved narrowly recorded owner exception (exact metric/allowance/evidence/reason/scope/expiry/follow-up), with the exception visible in the evidence and honest support/performance wording. The result remains an approved exception, not an unqualified pass. Safety allocation caps, dependency isolation, readiness/accessibility/focus, stale-work protection, discarded-object cleanup (including its 512 KiB residual ceiling) and bounded-resource behavior have no temporary waiver; a change returns as an explicit contract-revision decision. Missing evidence is unverified, not an exception that manufactures evidence. Baseline changes are versioned, reviewed and preserve history. Compare retained durable and last-release references; new entries use absolute caps/review, and zero-baseline invariants use their direct checks rather than percentages. Runtime confirmation retains the original and confirmatory valid sets; unresolved conflicts cannot be green by selecting a favorable rerun.

requirements.clause:
1. **Packed-artifact gate.** Build/pack, install outside workspace linking in vanilla/React/Next consumers, verify all entry exports/CSS/registration and type/runtime behavior, compare family/root selectivity and matched adapter increments. Measure all style modes, server closure separately and common combined graphs. No framework/dev-tool dependency in core and no dense imports in primitive use. Browser-free server/helper imports start no document resources.
2. **Manifest and reference gate.** Check in frozen manifest and build/compression/tool settings; verify hardware/browser/cache/cadence and actual visibility counts. Record missing prerequisites as unverified. Keep original/candidate/static reference artifacts and conditions, not just summaries. Compare renderer candidates at equivalent accepted quality before commitment.
3. **Phase and timing gate.** Capture cold import/registration, setup, active motion, handoff, static/inactive and cleanup separately. Use three warmups/twenty valid paired runs, declared percentiles/pooled and per-run tests, normal cadence floor, whole-page traces and independent 50ms task check. Benchmark arbitrary app/third-party code only in clearly separated application evidence; known fixture provider cost is visible.
4. **Bounded allocation and degradation gate.** Exercise every boundary and excess input, resize/temporary peaks, zero-size and context loss, document saturation across compatible copies, large lists/offscreen admission and stress. All resource ledgers/capacity limits hold before allocation. Typical fixture retains intended appearance; permitted stress degradation reports quality/cadence/active versus static counts. Every fallback preserves readiness/content/identity/focus/status and the four-second deadline.
5. **Idle/lifecycle/memory gate.** Verify no recurring decorative work in every inactive state, immediate current-state handling without stale backlogs, last-consumer teardown, all fixture disposal, three full cleanup experiments and every checkpoint. Include reconnect/Strict Mode/adoption and invalid/provider-error paths. Inspect retained objects and capacity alongside heap; unavailable memory APIs do not become invented zeroes or portable memory claims.
6. **SSR/layout/CSP gate.** Measure default/maximum raw markup, actual repeated-style gzip overhead and warm helper calls per Node/Bun runtime. Exercise ready/pending, initial HTML/streaming/hydration/client navigation, no/failed/delayed JS and failed upgrades. Check identity, fixed geometry/raw shift entries/complete CLS and application-owned no-JS recovery. Count assets honestly under actual CSP modes. Report Next/framework cost separately.
7. **Regression/release evidence gate.** Enforce hard limits and conjunction regression thresholds against durable and last-release records, with one predefined confirmatory protocol and no cherry-picking. Every required item is pass/fail/unverified or a clearly identified permitted numeric exception. Record artifact/commit/date/device/OS/browser/runtime/tool versions, manifest, raw trace/results/size reports, fallback counts, findings, exception links and limitations. Missing or failed evidence blocks the affected claim. Run the full selected suite for launch; later changes rerun affected measurements with retained evidence only where still comparable. Website Web Vitals remain separate page goals; field p75 is not inferred from lab results, and no telemetry is added by this plan.

requirements.clause:
1. **Choreography and visual fidelity.** Retain a versioned fixture/recording baseline for every first-party advertised idle/handoff combination, meaningful option endpoints and representative simultaneous surfaces. Human review at normal speed verifies geometry convergence, skeleton disappearance, actual-content reveal, continuity, timing and static fallbacks. Slower/frozen inspection supplements normal-speed review. Cover line/bar/scatter final geometry, supported numeric/label text and table cell/row types. Record layout, dataset/seed, font, direction, dimensions, DPR and preferences. No generic fade substituted for an advertised specialized treatment without explicit disclosure/review. No claim of pixel-identical m37 parity.
2. **Packed public contract.** Native and React/Next consumers use actual packed JS/types/CSS, supported minimum/current tooling and environments. Positive and negative type fixtures cover every exported factory, helper, family, phase, option and inferred prepared state. Test property/pre-upgrade/atomic update, preset precedence and override removal. Compile/run complete docs examples, including independent custom idle/handoff definitions. Selective import checks must show no unrelated family/framework runtime. No undeclared helper or callback-string execution.
3. **Readiness, interruption and events.** Deterministic tests cover every state transition, equivalent configuration, captured options/timing, live idle/speed changes, geometry invalidation, reentrant event handlers, supersession, removal/adoption and rapid updates. Every committed start has exactly one end/cancel; obsolete work has no later mutation/completion. Test complete totals, zero, easing and four-second elapsed deadline against actually displayed motion, including main-thread stalls/compositor effects. Preserve existing immediate failure/cancellation recipe and skipped-versus-committed event semantics.
4. **Application content and target ownership.** Real native/React content retains identity, handlers, state, focus and application styles. Test valid, missing, conflicting, outside, nested-owner, removed, reordered and virtualized row targets; enforce100 targets independently of geometry caps. Focusable controls must be available at readiness without waiting for decorative completion. Exercise the three clarifications below, app style/animation changes and cancellation cleanup. No cloned content, arbitrary selector discovery or required grid/chart runtime.
5. **Accessibility, preferences and actual environments.** Extend the approved floor/current-browser, real-device, genuine Windows forced-colors, live OS reduced-motion, persistent website pause and manual screen-reader matrices to the motion/target paths. Test keyboard/focus, decorative semantics, no false progress, status independence, contrast/flashing at supported speed/option extremes, zoom/text spacing and international content. Resized viewports and zero automated scan violations cannot replace the established manual evidence.
6. **Static rendering, security policy and fallbacks.** Packed server imports are DOM-free; functions/element references are never serialized into HTML or share links. Test pending/ready/streaming/delayed or failed upgrade, hydration and client navigation under actual supported CSP headers/style delivery modes and Trusted Types enforcement. Invalid/oversized/throwing geometry/options/definitions use bounded diagnostics and safe presentation; no permissive-policy workaround, stuck hidden result or retry loop. Test missing/failed canvas resources and valid updates after recovery.
7. **Measured resources and regressions.** Apply all existing numerical bundle, frame/setup, backing-pixel, dot/geometry, allocation, heap, SSR/CLS and cleanup budgets to actual distributables and claimed motion catalog. Include known custom-definition fixtures in the same runner and report their cost; never promise to sandbox/preempt arbitrary user JavaScript. Use the approved physical Pixel reference and secondary devices, fixed workloads, paired baselines, three warmups/twenty valid runs and retained evidence. Test allowed worst-case settings, fallbacks, multiple compatible copies and zero dormant scheduling. Numerical exceptions follow existing narrowly scoped governance; readiness/focus/safety/stale-work/cleanup invariants cannot be waived.

requirements.clause:
- **C1 — Focus wins over decorative reveal.** If focus enters content still constrained by opacity/clip/row choreography, immediately settle the entire owning handoff to its latest valid presentation, remove its scoped effects and preserve focus. Do not wait for a row delay or make ready content inert merely to preserve animation. Settlement ends a still-current committed handoff; supersession/removal still cancels it.
- **C2 — A stale visual plan cannot survive content invalidation.** A normal configuration edit stays next-handoff-only. But a supplied-content/measurement change that invalidates captured geometry, removal/recycling of a captured target or conflicting ownership during playback immediately settles latest valid ready content and clears old effects. Do not replan/replay mid-handoff or rearm motion. App-owned removal of a focused node remains the app's focus-management responsibility. Target-list updates without invalidating current targets apply next time.
- **C3 — Completion is exact despite easing or author output.** Expose bounded eased progress alongside raw linear progress; easing never extends the total or four-second deadline. At completion the engine removes decoration and owned effects and makes the full latest valid content presentation available, even if a custom author omitted a final reveal command.
